Take a small quantity of acetic acid in a test tube and smell it. It emits an irritating pungent odour. Keep the mouth of the test tube away from both your and your classmates' faces.
Put a small quantity of acetic acid in one test tube and a small quantity of distilled water in another test tube.
Add acetic acid to the water.
Shake the test tube well.
A homogeneous solution is formed.
Take a strip of blue litmus paper.
Dip it in a test tube containing a small quantity of acetic acid.
Blue litmus turns red, showing that acetic acid is acidic in nature.
Put a small quantity of sodium bicarbonate solution in a boiling tube.
Clamp the boiling tube to a stand.
Close the mouth of the boiling tube with a double bored cork.
Insert a thistle funnel into the tube through one of the holes in the cork.
Take another boiling tube containing lime water.
Clamp this boiling tube to another stand.
Take a delivery tube and insert one end in the tube containing sodium bicarbonate (through the hole in the cork) and the other end in the tube containing lime water.
Take a bottle containing acetic acid.
Pour the acetic acid through the thistle funnel into the boiling tube containing sodium bicarbonate.
A gas evolves.
The lime water in the boiling tube turns milky.
The gas evolved is CO[sub]2[/sub] which turns lime water milky.
